# Proving a claim producer before you ship it

`rimsky conformance claim-producer` drives your producer over the published
protocol and prints one pass/fail row per check. You need your producer running
and the shipped CLI — no deployment, no container.

## Run it

```bash
rimsky conformance claim-producer \
  --endpoint grpc://127.0.0.1:9401 \
  --timeout 60s
```

## An honest producer passes

The suite draws 16 checks and reports one `ok` row each, covering the
capabilities handshake, the first Open, the four terminal verbs, the three
retried-terminal idempotency checks, and the serialization probe:

```
ok    Capabilities
ok    OpenFirst
ok    Commit
ok    Abandon
ok    Release
ok    TerminalIdempotency
ok    AbandonTerminalIdempotency
ok    ReleaseTerminalIdempotency
ok    Serialization9b
```

The command exits 0.

## A failing producer is told which checks failed

Point the same suite at a producer that rejects a retried terminal verb.
Exactly the three retry checks fail, each named:

```
FAIL  TerminalIdempotency
FAIL  AbandonTerminalIdempotency
FAIL  ReleaseTerminalIdempotency
ok    Commit
ok    Abandon
ok    Release
3/16 checks failed
```

Each failure names the producer's rejection and states that terminal verbs must
be idempotent under retry. The first-call rows still report ok, so the report
separates "your Commit works" from "your Commit is not idempotent under retry".
The command exits 1.

## The serialization probe keeps advertised semantics honest

Point the suite at a producer that advertises `staged_async` write semantics
while quietly blocking a reader behind a writer on the same scope. Exactly one
check fails:

```
FAIL  Serialization9b
1/16 checks failed
```

The message names the reader-lease pattern as forbidden for `staged_async` and
says what honest support would require. Every other row, including the terminal
verbs, still reports ok, and the command exits 1.

This is the check a producer's own tests would not catch, because the producer
believes its own advertisement.
